key_insight: PPG-LM learns from both PPG waveforms and EHR context to align physiological signals with clinically grounded language at segment, event, and visit levels.
clinical_relevance: This could improve wearable and monitor-based assessment by making PPG more interpretable for retrieval, captioning, and clinical prediction tasks.
method: Built an automatic captioning pipeline to generate segment-, event-, and visit-level descriptions from PPG measurements and structured EHR data.
Used a two-stage framework: contrastive learning plus waveform-conditioned captioning, then temporal aggregation and statement matching for higher-level alignment.
Pretrained on about 73k hours of PPG to support language-based recognition, cross-modal retrieval, and segment captioning.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on MC-MED, MIMIC-III, and VitalDB, where it improved retrieval and caption factuality over language-model baselines and showed gains on multiple clinical prediction tasks.
watch_item: Clinical captions and temporal alignment depend on automatically generated labels, so errors in EHR-derived descriptions or mismatched timing could affect real-world reliability.
paper_title: PPG-LM: A Photoplethysmography-Language Model with Multi-Level Clinical Alignment
